Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

South Wales Police recorded 358 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 7.5 per 1,000 residents, the 19th highest rate of Cardiff's 28 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (13), vehicle crime (4), burglary (2); the evening/night score by violent crime (34), anti social behaviour (28), public order (18). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Whitchurch and Tongwynlais safe?

Wandroz currently rates Whitchurch and Tongwynlais in Cardiff as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Cardiff during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Cardiff at night. This rating is derived from South Wales Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Whitchurch and Tongwynlais safe at night?

At night, Whitchurch and Tongwynlais is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Cardiff. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Whitchurch and Tongwynlais a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Whitchurch and Tongwynlais's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Cardiff) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
